normalized.description: Objectives: To consolidate alternative solutions for on-board loss minimization. To develop the prototypes of the most relevant solutions identified, to confirm the predicted performance. To provide road-map to flight models. The state of art TTC Sub-System architectures for Science and Exploration missions are nowadays quite complex. In order to allow communications during all mission phases, several antennas are needed in combination with redundant High Power Amplifiers (HPA) and transponders (DST). The interconnectionamong these components is accomplished by the RF Distribution Unit (RFDU), which has to guarantee the maximum degree of reconfigurability and reliability to failures. In addition, it has also to implement the necessary filtering action, to allow full duplex communications. Its design is therefore quite complex encompassing the use of several switches, Diplexers, Filters and interconnecting waveguides (WG) runs. The latter can be quite long as they have to reach antennas which are typically far from the location of the rest of the TTC subsystem. All this results in high losses with RF power reduction in transmission and increased noise figure in reception.The design solutions used so far in the frame of ESA projects are quite recurrent with no major improvements in the last decades. As shown in a TTC Sub-System architecture survey carried out in 2017, different approaches exist, as identified for example by other agencies and already flown successfully in the past years. For a complex RFDU as used in Deep Space missions, we can consider RF path losses in the order of 1 to 3 dB in X-band and 3 to 4 dB in Ka-band, withsignificant impacts in terms of data return (up to50% reduction) and in terms of spacecraft recovery possibilities in case of anomalies (increasedoperations complexity and limitation on maximum achievable distance). Therefore, there is a clear need for loss reduction in the RFDU paths, through the implementation of novel solutions. A study is on-going to consolidate the possible alternative subsystem Architectures, and define relevant requirements. This will be completed in early 2024, but its conclusions need to be consolidated by experimental results. The activity shall focus on the specification, detailed design, development and tests of prototypes of the components which will have the most significant impact on the TTC subsystem performance and whose feasibility has to be demonstrated. Three main items have been already identified, which may need to be completed by additional technologies as an outcome of the on-going study:- Receiving only antenna with integrated low-noise-amplifier (LNA) and downconverter (D/C), with a possible alternative for a receiving and transmitting solution;- High-gain-antenna dual-band feed including receiving LNA and D/C, and with direct interface to power amplifier;- Transponder front-end to manage the interfaces with new antennas designs.Tasks:1. Consolidation of requirements and design2. Design and manufacturing of bread-boards3. Testing of bread-boards4. Development plan for flight models.

normalized.title: INCUBED-2 STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL
normalized.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims at accompanying the European economic operators in the Earth Observation market rapid evolution currently witnessed in Europe and overseas. InCubed offers a new process in ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the realization of endeavours near-to-the-market with Economic Operators. Activities to be supported include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (missions, instruments, prototype element of EO constellation), innovative mission management solution, including for future EO constellation, the development of application platforms, etc. InCubed is looking for commercial viability by the end of the activity (up to at least a minimum viable product level) and a substantial degree of innovation i.e. adding new value to the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement/involvement is mandatory. Commercial customers are encouraged to be either as part of the consortium representing the value chain or as beta testers/validators of the developed product/service.  Customer engagement/involvement must be highlighted at the pitch and proposal stage. Letters of potential customer support/interest are seen as a very positive aspect. The actual scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves in relevance to the InCubed objectives. Two development cycles are possible within InCubed: TheDe-Risking Cycle (start TRL 4) and Product Development Cycle (startTRL 6) depending on the maturity of the concept being developed. Regarding this forthcoming Announcement of Partnership Opportunity, Economic operators are invited to register and submit idea pitches onto ideas.esa.int (InCubed channel). Following a positive pitch meeting, the second step is to fill in a Part 1 (Outline) proposal template, which must be supported by the Participating State(s) having jurisdiction over them. Following a positive assessment,the economic operators will be invited to submit a Part 2 (Full) proposal template, as per established procedure and evaluation criteria. The proposals to be supported by InCubed will have to be co-funded by the economic operators (partnership agreements), as a sign of their engagement and belief in their own business case.

This procedure follows a two-steps procurement approach:-Step 1 - Qualification Phase: Qualification process established through an Open Competition (Frame Invitation To Tender - Frame ITT) resulting in the award of Frame Contracts between the Agency and several service providers. normalized.title: INCUBED CALL FOR PROPOSAL: STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
normalized.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims to accompany European economic operators in the rapid evolution of the Earth Observation market, both in Europe and globally. InCubed introduces a dedicated process within ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the development of near-to-market commercial initiatives in partnership with industry. Activities supported under InCubed include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (e.g. missions, instruments, prototype elements of EO constellations), innovative mission management solutions (including for future EO constellations), as well as the development of ground, data, and application platforms. InCubed targets commercial viability by the end of the activity (at least at minimum viable product level) and requires a substantial degree of innovation, i.e. the creation of new value within the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement is mandatory, with customers acting as beta testers and validators of the developed product or service. Customer engagement must be clearly demonstrated at both pitch and proposal stages, and letters of support or interest from potential customers are considered a strong asset. The scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves, in line with the objectives of InCubed. Two development cycles are available within InCubed, depending on the maturity of the concept: De-risking Cycle (typically starting from TRL 4), focusing on reducing technical and market risks;Product Development Cycle (typically starting from TRL 6), aiming at delivering a product ready for commercialisation. Under this Call for Proposals, economic operators are invited to submit their ideas via the OSIP (Open Space Innovation Platform) (ideas.esa.int), which serves as the entry point for the programme. The application process consists of the following step: Idea Pitch - Applicantssubmit and present a draft Outline proposal via OSIP to ESA (and potentially the relevant National Delegation(s)). Following a positive assessment, economic operators will be invited to submit a Proposal Part 2 (Full) in accordance with the established procedures and evaluation criteria. Activities supported under InCubed are based on a co-funding scheme, whereby economic operators contribute financially to the project, demonstrating commitment to and confidence in their business case.

{"job":"national-NO-DOFFIN-ANNOUNCEMENT_OF_COMPETITION","collectionState":"reconciled","verifiedOpen":false,"spaceRelevance":"not_assessed","recordType":"institution_discovery_candidate","extracted":{"reference":"2026-115893","title":"Kompetansemeglere for forskningsmobilisering i Troms","description":"Bakgrunn

Troms fylkeskommune, ved FORREGION Troms i seksjon utvikling og innovasjon, har behov for ekstern bistand til forskningsmobilisering i næringslivet. Formålet er å styrke koblingen mellom bedrifter og relevante forsknings- og utviklingsmiljøer, og bidra til at flere virksomheter i Troms igangsetter forsknings- og innovasjonsprosjekter.

FORREGION står for forskningsbasert innovasjon i regionene og er en tilskuddsordning rettet mot bedrifter med liten eller ingen erfaring med forskning og utviklingsarbeid. Anskaffelsen skal understøtte ordningens mål om å øke andelen FoU i næringslivet gjennom mobilisering, tettere kobling mellom næringsliv og FoU-miljøer og at forprosjekter i større grad leder videre til hovedprosjekter og annen videreført forskningsaktivitet.

Anskaffelsen gjennomføres fordi fylkeskommunen har behov for kapasitet og spisskompetanse til å arbeide systematisk, oppsøkende og behovsstyrt overfor bedrifter, særlig små og mellomstore virksomheter som i liten grad har erfaring med forskning og utvikling. Det er samtidig et behov for å gjøre relevante FoU-miljøer, finansieringsordninger og øvrige virkemidler mer tilgjengelige for næringslivet i regionen.

Oppdraget skal støtte målsettingen om økt forskningsinnsats i næringslivet, flere kvalifiserte søknader til relevante forskningsmidler og bedre regional dekning i mobiliseringsarbeidet. Det er særlig viktig å mobilisere forskningsumodne bedrifter i prioriterte bransjer, legge til rette for flere varige samarbeidsrelasjoner mellom næringsliv og FoU-aktører og bidra til videreføring av lovende initiativer fra tidlig idéfase og forprosjekt til større utviklings- og forskningsprosjekter.

Beskrivelse av oppdraget

Oppdragsgiver skal anskaffe bistand fra totalt fem kompetansemeglerteam til forskningsmobilisering i Troms. Ressursene skal samlet dekke temaområdene sjømat, romvirksomhet/space, KI og teknologiutvikling samt Sirkulære Troms, hvor to av delkontraktene skal være knyttet til sjømat. Hver delkontrakt skal ivaretas av et kompetansemeglerteam med relevant og komplementær kompetanse innen aktuelt innsatsområde.

Målgruppen for oppdraget er små og mellomstore bedrifter som tilhører Troms fylke, eller som har betydelig aktivitet i Troms. Kompetansemegling skal være et gratis tilbud til målgruppen. Oppdraget forutsetter at kompetansemeglerne opptrer uavhengig og nøytralt, og at de ikke representerer næringsaktører som kan stå i et konkurranseforhold til bedriftene som mottar bistand. Kompetansemeglere skal signere taushetserklæring.

Leveransen omfatter oppsøkende kontakt med bedrifter, behovsanalyse, kartlegging av relevante FoU-partnere, kobling mellom bedrifter og forskningsmiljøer samt veiledning i utvikling av FoU-prosjekter og søknader om forskningsmidler. Oppfølgingen skal tilpasses den enkelte bedrifts behov og modenhet, og kan omfatte bistand fra tidlig idéavklaring og forprosjekt til videre mobilisering mot hovedprosjekter og andre relevante ordninger. Kompetansemegler skal være rådgiver og veileder i søknadsprosesser, men skal ikke skrive søknader på vegne av bedriftene eller opptre i konkurranse med private aktører.

Kompetansemeglerteamene skal kunne identifisere virksomheters behov for forskning og innovasjon, bidra til å finne relevant forskningskompetanse og veilede bedriftene mot hensiktsmessige finansieringskilder. Dette inkluderer FORREGION og andre aktuelle ordninger, eksempelvis SkatteFUNN, Norges forskningsråd, Innovasjon Norge, Horisont Europa og andre relevante virkemidler. Der det er naturlig, skal kompetansemeglerne også henvise videre til andre aktører i virkemiddelapparatet.

Oppdraget omfatter videre oppfølging av bedrifter som tidligere har gjennomført forprosjekter finansiert av FORREGION Troms, med mål om å bidra til videre utvikling og gjennomføring av hovedprosjekter. Kompetansemeglerne skal også kunne arrangere nettverksmøter mellom næringsliv og FoU-aktører for å identifisere felles problemstillinger, muligheter for forskning og utvikling samt styrke kunnskapsdeling og samarbeid.
